newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's FTC to try to simplify merger procedures.
newsitem.headline: Japan's FTC to try to simplify merger procedures.

text.p: Japan's fair trade watchdog said on Thursday it would try to simplify procedures for corporate mergers and bring them more in line with international standards following a recommendation by an advisory panel.

An official of the Fair Trade Commission (FTC) told Reuters the body would honour the latest recommendation submitted by a study group comprised of scholars, journalists, and corporate presidents, but stopped short of saying what specific measures would be taken.
"We are not yet in a position to make public any specific plans now," the official said.
Japan's strict anti-monopoly rules have been a stumbling block for large companies seeking to boost their international competitiveness through mergers.

The panel urged the FTC to simplify procedures by requiring prior application for mergers only in cases where a company with assets of more than 10 billion yen merges with a company with assets of more than one billion yen.
By doing so, the number of applications filed to the FTC would drop by about 90 percent from the current level of about 2,300 cases a year.
Last month, the FTC said it received a total of 2,271 merger filings in the year to March, the second-largest number on record following the previous year's 2,520 cases.
The panel also recommended dropping application requirements for mergers between small companies as well as for those between subsidiaries belonging to the same company group.
It also urged the FTC to ease current requirements for companies and individuals to report their share holdings in other companies once a year.
The FTC official said the report was largely in line with what the FTC had expected and that the changes following the proposals were likely to be made as early as next year.
